Religion supplies a moral standard outside social consensus, enabling prophetic criticism of accepted injustice and giving the powerful reasons to restrain exploitation when self-interest favors it.
The move states the principal theistic objection to conventional secular morality: reciprocity and social order may not justify resistance to entrenched norms or constrain beneficiaries of injustice.
Pinker's claim that consistency, reciprocity, moral self-conception, and cooperative welfare adequately explain why people should be moral.
